correctness.rationale: The rational generating identity M_n(z)=sum a^n z^a=∑j!S(n,j)z^j/(1−z)^{j+1} and F_n=(1/2)M_n(1/2) are standard. Coefficientwise Euler divisibility at p∤a and a=pb shows M_{n+P}(z)−M_n(z)+p^n M_n(z^p) has all coefficients in p^k Z; clearing unit-constant rational denominators evaluates at 1/2 in Z_(p). The R congruence and R≡F_n mod p follow. The proof of minimal preperiod uses any putative period d and a large d-multiple to transfer the P-shift backward; it does not assume P the only possible period. Modulo 3, F_n≡2^n−1 for n≥1 gives odd-index units and even-index divisibility; k−1/k−2 boundaries yield parity law, with k=1 and n=0 treated. Independent bounded grids corroborate.

final_claim: Ordered Bell numbers F_n satisfy F_{n+(p−1)p^{k−1}}−F_n ≡ −p^n R_{p,n} (mod p^k), where R_{p,n}=2^{p−1}∑ j!S(n,j)/(2^p−1)^{j+1}; the least preperiod is determined by the finite failing-index set and s(3,k)=1 (k=1), k (even k), k−1 (odd k>=3).
